{{Quote|No one controls a Queen of the Quesoth. ''[&hellip;]'' It is she who controls.''"<br />"''Which you should have realized from the beginning. ''[&hellip;]'' How else do you think that Circling was actually willing to pretend to treason? He acted that way under his Queen's orders so that he could persuade you to take the pictures I wanted Thrawn to have.|The Queen of the Red and Warlord Nuso Esva, to bowlcarrier Trevik|<ref name="Crisis of Faith" />}}
The '''Quesoth''' were a [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Insectoid/Legends|insectoid]] [[Species/Legends|species]] [[Homeworld/Legends|native]] to the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Quethold]] and spoke the [[Quesoth Common Speak]] [[Language/Legends|language]]. Divided by castes, several races followed the reigning Quesoth [[Queen/Legends|Queen]], the [[Queen of the Red]], [[Queen of the White|White]], or [[Queen of the Black|Black]], which changed periodically, blindly. The [[Quesoth Soldier]]s, who understood the [[Quesoth Soldier Speak]] tongue spoken by their monarch, the [[Midli]] caste&mdash;who oversaw the [[Workers (Quesoth)|Workers]]&mdash;and the [[Circling]], a caste composed by several subgroups formed by the Queen's advisers and [[Reproduction/Legends|breeders]], carried their Queens across their respective [[City/Legends|cities]]: the [[Red City]], the [[White City]], or the [[Black City]].

In an attempt to rule forever, the reigning [[Queen of the Red (8 ABY)|Queen of the Red]] in [[8 ABY/Legends|8 ABY]] allied herself with [[Storm-hair|alien]] [[Warlord/Legends|warlord]] [[Nuso Esva]]&mdash;whose species were nicknamed the "Storm-hairs" by the Quesoth&mdash;and promised to help [[Gender/Legends|him]] in his [[Nuso Esva's conquests|campaign]] against the [[Empire of the Hand]] and [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn]]. The warlord promised to [[Death/Legends|murder]] the future Queen of the White, allowing the Queen of the Red to rule, while she would allow him to use the manufacturing facilities beneath the White City after capturing the location with the [[juggernaut]]s they would steal from Thrawn. Unfortunately for her, during a [[Attack on the Red City|battle]] against the Grand Admiral's forces, Esva killed her fearing [[Treason/Legends|treason]].

==Biology and appearance==
{{Quote|You've never faced Quesoth Soldiers in battle. We, on the other hand, have dealt with them both as allies and as enemies. They're bigger even than the Workers-when they rear up they're nearly as tall as you or I-and immensely strong. They're also fiercely loyal to their Queen, obeying her orders unquestioningly and with no consideration for their own safety. And there are thousands of them within the Red City.|Stromma Council Liaison Nyama on the Quesoth Soldiers|<ref name="Crisis of Faith" />}}
[[File:Thrawn-SWM.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Grand Admiral Thrawn, who defeated Nuso Esva and the Queen of the Red's forces and was nearly as tall as a Quesoth Soldier.]]
The Quesoth, an [[Insectoid/Legends|insectoid]] [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]], had two abdomens and six [[Limb/Legends|limbs]]: two arms and four legs. Members of the species had [[Color/Legends|blue]]&ndash;colored [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] and the [[Quesoth Soldier]]s were nearly as tall as [[Empire of the Hand]] [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn]],<ref name="Crisis of Faith" /> who stood at 1.8 [[Meter/Legends|meters]],<ref name="TNEGtC">''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref> and strong according to [[Stromma Council Liaison]] [[Nyama]]. The Soldiers followed their [[Queen/Legends|Queen]] unquestioningly, while the Quesoth within the [[Midli]] and [[Circling]] castes&mdash;which oversaw [[Workers]] and advised the Queen and [[Reproduction/Legends|bred]] more members of the insectoid species&mdash;could think on their own and could handle equipment in a limited capacity. The Quesoth Soldiers understood their [[Quesoth Soldier Speak]] [[Language/Legends|language]], which their monarchs exclusively spoke thanks to their unique set of vocal cords and resonance cavities, while the rest spoke [[Quesoth Common Speak]].<ref name="Crisis of Faith" />

==Society and culture==
{{Dialogue|Queen of the Red|The old ways are at an end, Trevik of the Midli of the Seventh of the Red. ''[&hellip;]'' Why should I accept death for myself and my city merely because the Queen of the White has arisen? ''[&hellip;]''<nowiki></nowiki>|Trevik|But- ''[&hellip;]'' But the old Queen always dies when the new Queen arises and the air changes. It's the way of the world.|Nuso Esva|You're a naïve fool. ''[&hellip;]'' A Queen-a true Queen-doesn't simply sit back and accept the way of the world. ''[&hellip;]'' A true Queen grasps the world by the throat and squeezes her own destiny from it. Understand?|Trevik|No. ''[&hellip;]'' But I do understand one thing: the Queen of the White cannot arise if the Circlings of the white are dead. ''[&hellip;]'' If they are murdered.|attr=The Queen of the Red, bowlcarrier Trevik, and Warlord Nuso Esva|src=<ref name="Crisis of Faith" />}}
The Quesoth were ruled by a Queen, and their society was divided by castes, which were divided by smaller ones. The Circling were divided into two subcastes, the [[Circling of the Red]]&mdash;the Circlings in the [[Red City]] ruled by the [[Queen of the Red]]&mdash;the [[Circling of the White]], from the [[White City]]. The Circling of the Red had seven subgroups, one of which was the [[Circling of the First of the Red]], of which Circling [[Borosiv]] was part of. The Midli caste was likewise divided, with the [[Midli of the Seventh of the Red]] being the lowest one socially. The highest position a Midli could achieve was the position of [[bowlcarrier]], which was occupied by the Quesoth who carried an ornated bowl of [[Nectar/Legends|nectar]] for their Queen.<ref name="Crisis of Faith" />

The [[Queen of the Quesoth|Queens of the Quesoth]] changed periodically, with the Circlings, Midlis, Soldiers, and Workers traveling to the next city to live with their new Queen. The Queen of the Red ruled the Red City, and once she [[Death/Legends|died]] and the "air changes," her people&mdash;excluding the Circling of the Red, who would stay in the Red City's [[Palace (Red City)|citadel]] and breed a new Queen that would arise once the Queen of the White and the [[Queen of the Black]] died&mdash;traveled to the next city.<ref name="Crisis of Faith" /> In [[8 ABY/Legends|8 ABY]],<ref name="TERC">The events of ''[[Crisis of Faith]]'' take place in [[8 ABY/Legends|8 ABY]] according to ''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]''.</ref> the Queen of the Red's reign would end, and she would die, in two [[10 ABY/Legends|years]].<ref name="Crisis of Faith" />

==History==
{{Quote|When the battle is over and Thrawn has lost, he will leave. ''[&hellip;]'' He'll have no choice. His defeat here by primitives will severely damage the reputation that holds his fragile coalition together, and he and his star caravan will need to travel to other conflicts to take personal charge of those battles. Once he's gone, we'll take our newly captured vehicles to the White City. The Queen of the Red will become the Queen of Quethold ''[&hellip;]'' and I will have free access to the industrial facilities beneath the White City. There I will construct vehicles in which I and my Chosen may leave this world and once again carry the war to my enemies.|Warlord Nuso Esva, to bowlcarrier Trevik|<ref name="Crisis of Faith" />}}
In [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]],<ref name="TERCOC">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' dates the events of ''[[Choices of One]]'' to [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]].</ref> [[Captain of the Line/Legends|Senior Captain]] Thrawn shared [[Storm-hair|alien]] [[Warlord/Legends|warlord]] [[Nuso Esva]]'s boasts with the Quesoth through the [[DeepWater-class light freighter|''DeepWater'' freighter]] ''[[Lost Reef]]''{{'s}} [[Comm unit/Legends|comm]] in an attempt to prevent them from joining Esva.<ref name="Choices of One">''[[Choices of One]]''</ref> In 8 ABY,<ref name="TERC" /> however, the [[Queen of the Red (8 ABY)|reigning]] Queen of the Red allied herself with Esva, whose species were nicknamed "Storm-hairs" by the people of the Red City. Esva would capture Thrawn's [[juggernaut]]s which he would bring to the White City, there, he would break the city's barriers and would murder its ruler, allowing his ally to rule forever. With control of Quethold, the monarch would allow him to use the manufacturing facilities between the settlement to build [[Starship/Legends|ships]] so his [[Chosen (Nuso Esva)|Chosen]] [[Soldier/Legends|warriors]] and him could leave and bring war to their enemies.<ref name="Crisis of Faith" />

[[File:Aurek_7_FB.jpg|thumb|left|300px|The Imperial stormtroopers, which fought the Quesoth]]
The bowlcarrier, [[Trevik]], served nectar for her Queen while her entourage entered the [[Dwelling of Guests]] building, where a [[Unidentified Chosen (Quethold)|Chosen]] pledged his life to her, as mandated by Quesoth custom, and the Queen of the Red and her ally spoke about the destruction of Grand Admiral Thrawn. On his way [[Trevik's home|home]], Trevik was intercepted by a [[Unidentified Circling|Circling]], who brought him to the [[Circling ring]] of the Red City, where [[Jirvin]]&mdash;Trevik's [[Trevik's family|brother]] and the overseer of the Workers who managed electricity in the city&mdash;told him to record the artwork Esva had brought to the Dwelling so that it could be shared with Thrawn. With the art, the Chiss would be able to determine whether or not the Queen of the Red was a willing ally of Esva, and unbeknownst to the bowlcarrier, the warlord would gain the upper hand in the coming battle, as Thrawn would devise his tactics according to the artwork brought to him.<ref name="Crisis of Faith" />

Trevik accepted, and recorded Esva's paintings, bringing the recordings to Jirvin in the afternoon. The next [[Standard day/Legends|day]], the [[Attack on the Red City|battle]] between Esva's Chosen, the Soldiers, and Thrawn's juggernauts and [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] began. The Quesoth forces overwhelmed the stormtroopers, who hid inside buildings while a group of Soldiers rushed to the juggernauts to capture them. [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|Imperial starfighters]] flew over the cities, destroying or deactivating the [[Speaker/Legends|speakers]] used to transmit the Queen's orders in Quesoth Soldier Speak, as a normal [[Comlink/Legends|comlink]] could not transmit them. Trevik was informed by the Queen of the Red&mdash;who was discussing the battle with her ally within the Dwelling of Guests&mdash;that she knew he was a [[Treason/Legends|traitor]], but when Thrawn was able to modify the speakers to send an order commanding the Soldiers to protect Esva, the Storm-hair did not know of the order's meaning, and killed the Queen fearing treason. He was killed shortly after, as were his Chosen.<ref name="Crisis of Faith" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|If given the chance they may choose to become your allies, as have the Stomma and Quesoth.''"<br />"''Allies? ''[&hellip;]'' You have allies, Thrawn. All to me except the Chosen are mere tools. They can be useful tools, or they can be broken tools.''"<br />"''Interesting, ''[&hellip;]'' I imagine the Stomma and Quesoth leadership will be interested to learn what their true positions will be should they choose to join your realm.|Warlord Nuso Esva and Senior Captain Thrawn in ''Choices of One''|<ref name="Choices of One" />}}
The Quesoth were first mentioned in [[Timothy Zahn]]'s novel ''[[Choices of One]]'',<ref name="Choices of One" /> which was published on [[July 19]], [[2011]].<ref name="SW">{{PenguinRandomHouse|url=books/7858/choices-of-one-star-wars-legends-by-timothy-zahn|text=Choices of One: Star Wars Legends}}</ref> The species later made its full appearance in the novella Crisis of Faith, also written by Zahn<ref name="Crisis of Faith" /> and published on September 6 of the same year<ref name="COF">{{PenguinRandomHouse|url=books/211558/heir-to-the-empire-star-wars-legends-by-timothy-zahn|text=Heir to the Empire: Star Wars Legends}}</ref> as part of the [[Heir to the Empire: The 20th Anniversary Edition|20th Anniversary Edition]] of the [[1991]] novel ''[[Heir to the Empire]]''.<ref name="Crisis of Faith" />
